tasks.short: Calculate marked quantities and file them.

steps.what: Mark dimensions, profile, and component specifications.
Calculate square footage and material quantities.
Review the calculated profile and quantities.

tasks.design: The technician marks the dimensions, the profile, and the component specifications. {SPREADSHEET} calculates square footage and material quantities only from those marks. They review the result and accept it. {DOCS} files that version. A figure they did not mark is not calculated. The sheet does not choose a specification.
tasks.previous_blocker: Marked lengths were keyed again into a calculator after they were already on the drawing.
tasks.enabler_now: A sheet can add dimensions the technician has already marked.
tasks.still_hard: Which dimension counts, and whether the quantity is the right one, stay with the technician.
tasks.human_edge: The technician marks and accepts. A sheet does not choose the specification.
tasks.altitude: Marking, reviewing, and accepting stay in full. Only the calculation of marked quantities and the filing of the accepted quantities are shorter.

reach.learn: The estimator does not mark the drawing

evidence.claim: A quantity can be calculated from dimensions the technician has marked. A figure they did not mark is not calculated.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a drawing is ready to measure and ends when the accepted quantities are filed. The technician marks and accepts. The sheet only calculates marks.

The fields are the dimension they marked, the profile name, the component, and the quantity. The technician produces the marks. The sheet produces the arithmetic. A blank mark is left blank and is not guessed.
The prior classes this task as automate. The steps disagree in part: the marking and the review stay. The calculation and the filing are the parts that move.
unknowns: Whether the drawing they measure already carries marks from an earlier takeoff.
Which components the office refuses to quantify until the technician marks them.
research_questions: Does the drawing they measure already carry marks from an earlier takeoff?
Which components does the office refuse to quantify until the technician marks them?

tasks.short: Review blueprints and file the requirements.

steps.what: Read project blueprints and structural specifications.
Review structural specifications for the structure.

tasks.design: The technician reviews the structural specifications and determines the dimensions and the material requirements. {DOCS} only opens the project blueprints, then files the requirements they accepted. Opening a blueprint is not the review. The system on the drawing is not decided by the file.
tasks.previous_blocker: The blueprint was hunted for in the folder before the technician could review it.
tasks.enabler_now: A blueprint the project file already holds can be opened by its name.
tasks.still_hard: What the structure requires, and which material it needs, stay with the technician.
tasks.human_edge: The technician determines the requirements. An opened blueprint does not.
tasks.altitude: The review and the determination stay in full. Only opening the blueprint and filing the accepted requirements are shorter.

reach.learn: The designer does not determine the material

evidence.claim: A stored activity or complaint can be listed. The technician writes the report or the reply.

A tool that assigns work from a worker's performance, or that decides a safety outcome, is not used here. The technician evaluates conformance. National building rules differ on who may certify the work. This file does not certify it.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a project blueprint is on file and ends when the accepted material requirements are filed. The technician reviews and determines. Opening the file is not the review.

The fields are project id, blueprint name, the dimension they determine, and the material. The file produces the blueprint. The technician produces the requirement. A requirement they did not determine is not filed.
The prior classes this task as amplify. The steps agree the review stays. The open and the filing are the parts that move.
unknowns: Whether structural specifications are already stored with the blueprint.

tasks.short: Draft drawings and file the accepted set.

steps.what: Read specifications the projects must meet.

tasks.design: The technician drafts the detailed dimensional drawings, designs the layouts, and ensures conformance to the specifications. {DOCS} only opens the specifications, then files the drawings they accepted. Nothing drafts a drawing and nothing generates a layout. Drawing-software time that already runs is not counted as their labour.
tasks.previous_blocker: The specification was opened by hunting the folder before they could draft.
tasks.enabler_now: A specification the project already holds can be opened by its name.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the drawing conforms stays with the technician who drafted it.
tasks.human_edge: The technician drafts. A file does not draw.
tasks.altitude: Drafting, designing the layouts, and checking conformance stay in full. Only opening the specification and filing the accepted drawings are shorter.

reach.learn: The designer does not draft this set

evidence.claim: A tool that assigns work from a worker's performance, or that decides a safety outcome, is not used here. The technician evaluates conformance. National building rules differ on who may certify the work. This file does not certify it.

assumptions: The workflow starts when specifications are on the project and ends when the accepted drawings are filed. The technician drafts and ensures conformance. Nothing generates a drawing.

The fields are project id, the specification clause, and the drawing name. The project file produces the specification. The technician produces the drawing. A drawing they did not accept is not filed.

unknowns: Whether the specification they draft against is already a stored clause.

tasks.short: Confer with the supervisor on the project.

steps.what: Confer with the supervisor on project details.
Determine plan preparation and acceptance testing.
Set the evaluation of field conditions.

tasks.design: The technician confers with the supervisor, determines plan preparation and acceptance testing, and sets the evaluation of field conditions. The call is not recorded. Nothing determines the details. Nothing sends a note of the call.
tasks.previous_blocker: The details were settled only by talking with the supervisor.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing in the record confers with the supervisor or evaluates the field.
tasks.still_hard: What the project needs, and how the field conditions are evaluated, stay in the conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The technician confers. A note does not determine the plan.
tasks.altitude: The conferring stays in full. There is no shorter step.

reach.task: Set project details with the technician

evidence.claim: This design does not score technicians and does not record calls. A list of open work is not a performance record.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a project detail is unsettled and ends when the technician and the supervisor have conferred. Nothing is sent. Zero incremental hours are justified because no step is removed and no upkeep is added.
There is no new field. The supervisor produces the direction. The technician produces the evaluation of field conditions. Calls are not recorded.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree: the conferring stays.
unknowns: Whether the supervisor expects the call to be recorded.
Which field conditions the office will not evaluate until both have seen the site.
